label: letter e input as the 3rd original token (t=2), gated by the first two tokens
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit (~0.03% of steps). It is almost entirely an input-e detector: 94% of activations (92% of mass) are on steps where the input is e, and 87% (82% of mass) are on e at t=2, i.e. e as the third original token. But only 11% of t=2 e steps fire, and whether one fires depends on the first two tokens. It is likely when the first token is z, r, o or i (7x lift), or when the first token is s, k, l or t and the second is w, c, a, d, l, v or k. The rest are small clusters: e re-entered at copy step t=5 in L=3 sequences (this includes the max activation, c e o <DEL> c [e]), a few m/t/1 inputs on the last copy step, and rare <DEL>. It does not fire at t=0, t=1 or t>=6 in the original phase, and almost never on letters other than e. I did not find what sets magnitude beyond the token context; the top activations are L=3 copy-phase e re-inputs.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=2 & in_tok=e (+5.48), in_tok=e (+3.82), L=3 & t=5 (+3.63), phase=2 & in_tok=m (+3.05), prev2_tok=z (+2.32), orig3=- (+2.12). Lower it: in_first=0 (-2.79), prev_tok=m (-2.00), prev2_tok=c (-1.55), orig0=n (-1.45).
